candidates: When clamping a dimension against a minimum size constant while a zoom/scale factor is in play, clamp in logical (unscaled) units first and then multiply by scale: `Math.max(MIN, logicalValue) * scale`. Do not clamp after scaling (i.e., avoid `Math.max(MIN, logicalValue * scale)`), because that applies the minimum in physical pixels — at non-1× zoom the displayed logical value on drag handles will fall below the intended minimum.

Avoid single-letter or terse abbreviated prefixes in local variable names (e.g. `nx`, `ny`, `ux`, `uy`, `vw`, `vh`). Use names that make the variable's role self-evident without needing to decode what the prefix stands for (e.g. `logicalWidth`, `widthUnit`, `scaledHeight`).

When using CSS custom properties to prevent Emotion from generating a new CSS class name on every dynamic value change, the accompanying inline comment should name the specific trigger (e.g. 'on every resize' or 'on every drag update') rather than vague phrasing like 'every possible value', so that the performance rationale is immediately clear to future readers.

When adding a non-obvious boolean or enum prop to a styled component, add or update a JSDoc comment on the component that explains what the prop controls, the behavioral or layout effect it has, and why it exists — particularly when the prop's default behavior is the more common case and the opt-out path is subtle.
